titular: Wall Street wraps up its best week since August despite a Friday dip
resum: The S&P 500 lost 0.4% on Friday to 7,561.67 points and the Nasdaq 0.9%, dragged down by tech stocks again. Even so, the S&P 500 gained 2.5% over the week, its first winning week since October, and the Dow Jones was the only major index to rise on Friday (+0.1%).
per_que_importa: Many pension plans and index funds track the S&P 500, so a week like this shows up in the savings of millions of people. It also shows that bad news at one big company doesn't necessarily drag the whole market down.

titular: European stocks hit another record and post their best week since June
resum: The Stoxx 600, which groups 600 large European companies, closed virtually flat on Friday (+0.02%) at a new high of 664.14 points, up 2.4% on the week. Germany's DAX slipped 0.08% as Infineon fell, but gained 3.6% for the week; oil majors and insurers offset the slide in chipmakers.
per_que_importa: When European stock markets rise, funds and pension plans that invest in the continent's companies gain value. The fact that the record was driven by sectors like energy and insurance shows Europe relies less on tech than the US does.

titular: Spain's Ibex gains 3.36% on the week and climbs back above 20,000
resum: Spanish stocks rose 0.27% on Friday to close at 20,020.1 points, after a cautious session amid the Nvidia hangover and tension with Iran. Over the week the index gained 3.36% and it is up 15.67% so far this year; Repsol was Friday's top gainer.
per_que_importa: The Ibex brings together Spain's 35 largest companies, such as banks, utilities and Inditex, which employ hundreds of thousands of people. When their shares rise, their shareholders, including many small savers, see their savings grow.

titular: Acciona plunges 7.98% as its asset sales are delayed
resum: Acciona shares fell 7.98% on Friday to €203 after the company admitted it will not reach this year's target of €2bn in asset sales because several deals have been delayed. Its subsidiary Acciona Energía fell 7.26%, although the group still expects to end the year at the top of its operating profit guidance (between €2.8bn and €3.1bn).
per_que_importa: Many companies sell parts of their business to cut debt and fund new investments, such as wind or solar farms. If those sales are delayed, the company has less room to invest, and the stock market punishes it right away.

titular: Spain confirms October inflation at 4.9%, the highest since February 2023
resum: The final figure from Spain's statistics office (INE) matches the flash estimate: prices are up 4.9% on a year earlier, the same as in September, and core inflation (excluding energy and fresh food) holds at 3.1%. Gas and tourism pushed prices up, while fuel held them back; the index used to update rents (IRAV) stands at 2.57%.
per_que_importa: With inflation at 4.9%, anyone whose salary isn't adjusted or whose savings earn no interest loses purchasing power every month. For tenants, the IRAV sets the maximum increase for many rental contracts when they are reviewed.

titular: US factory-gate prices rise 6.5% in a year, the most since 2022
resum: The producer price index, which measures what businesses charge for what they produce, rose 0.3% in October, slightly less than the 0.4% expected. Over a year, however, it is up 6.5%, the biggest increase since November 2022.
per_que_importa: When materials and energy get more expensive for businesses, they tend to pass part of that cost on to shop prices a few months later. That is why this figure is an early warning of where the inflation families pay may be heading.

titular: The US 10-year Treasury yield climbs to 5.15% and markets see a December rate hike as a done deal
resum: The yield on the 10-year US Treasury rose 5 basis points on Friday to above 5.15%, while markets put a 100% probability on the Federal Reserve (Fed) raising rates in December. Governor Chris Waller said he could support a half-point hike if core inflation keeps rising by 0.3% or more each month.
per_que_importa: The 10-year yield is a benchmark for mortgages, business loans and the debt of many countries. When it rises, borrowing becomes more expensive around the world, including in Europe.

titular: Hong Kong falls for a third day as tech stocks drop 3%
resum: The Hang Seng index fell 1.55% on Friday to 23,637.60 points, and Hong Kong's tech index slumped 3.02% on doubts about artificial intelligence. Lenovo lost 6.33% and chipmaker Hua Hong 6.10%.
per_que_importa: Asian markets are very sensitive to what happens with chips and AI, because the region makes much of the world's electronic components. When fear spreads there, it is felt in supply chains and in funds that invest in emerging markets.

titular: Oil ends a second week of declines but stays close to $96
resum: Brent finished Friday at $95.84 a barrel, almost unchanged from Thursday, posting a second weekly decline as traders weighed mixed signals on US-Iran talks. The International Energy Agency expects the market to have more oil than demand this quarter for the first time since the war began.
per_que_importa: The price of oil ends up in petrol, in the diesel trucks run on and in the bills of many industries. If the market has more supply than demand, it is a sign that pressure on those prices could ease.

titular: Next week: Nvidia's results and Anthropic's stock market debut
resum: Nvidia reports results on Tuesday 17th, after Wall Street closes, in the middle of its transition following Jensen Huang's exit. Anthropic is expected to price its IPO on Wednesday 18th and start trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday 19th; the US also publishes retail sales and industrial production.
per_que_importa: These are two of the most awaited events of the year for the stock market: Nvidia's results will show whether spending on AI is still growing, and Anthropic's debut will show how much investors are willing to pay for this business.
